cells.tense: What moves between people is warm at the moment, and you are the one keeping it that way.
cells.act: lay the one step you can see, solidly
cells.ask: Pick the relationship that actually moved this week and do its next errand — a call, a plan, a repair — well enough to hold. Keep it small enough to finish, and leave the rest alone.
cells.core:
You can sit with someone's hard feeling without climbing into it or leaving the chair. When you hold a room, people quit performing for each other and start saying the true thing; you aren't managing them, you're keeping things from falling apart. That's rare, and it's yours. What it wants isn't more tenderness — it's a piece of it finished.

Somewhere near you is a relationship genuinely in motion. Choose that one, not the most urgent one. Do the next actual thing it's asking for — one call, one plan, one repair — and lay it down solid. Keep it small enough to finish this week. The warmth you carry will keep; what it's missing is a stone under it, one you could point to if someone asked. Everything soft you hold gets steadier when a piece of it is done.
cells.sheetLine: You keep the warmth. Now finish a small piece of it.
cells.verb: tending the feeling between people so what's there has room to move and stay warm without dissolving into it
cells.place: the seed-state before anything has chosen its shape yet — everything still possible, nothing committed

cells.tense: The warmth between people will have to hold before anyone has actually said a word out loud.
cells.act: release what is done and keep what serves
cells.ask: Set down the upkeep on something that's finished — a role you keep replaying, a version of a friendship you keep feeding. Hold off it a week; put your hands on what still moves.
cells.core:
You are holding several relationships the way you'd hold them if they were about to break, and none of them is breaking at the moment. Every history gets kept warm ahead of time, every feeling managed before it arrives. From the seed-state where nothing has chosen its shape, that pre-holding becomes the whole of the work, and it's tiring in a way tending didn't use to be. The heat is real. Nothing is actually being warmed.

Something in that pile is already finished. Pick it out — a role you keep playing back into being, a version of a relationship you keep showing up to, an argument that's done its work. Use the week to stop feeding it. What is still truly alive gets your hands instead, and you'll feel the difference quickly. Setting down a finished thing isn't losing it. It's how the living part stays fed.

cells.tense: Sitting with what someone feels used to be something you could do without leaving yourself behind.
cells.act: say the hard thing gently, once
cells.ask: Tell the person who should hear it the true sentence — plainly, kindly, once. No rehearsal, no cleaning it up after, and no leaving right away.
cells.core:
The place where you could sit beside someone's feeling has gone quiet, and you've been standing out in the hallway. You're still kind. The trouble is timing: you keep arriving after the feeling has passed, or before it lands — agreeing quickly, keeping the evening light, not claiming the part where you're with them while it hurts. Nobody sent you out there. It's just easier now to be the one who doesn't need to be in it.

There's something true you've held back from someone. Say it once, gently, and then stop — no rehearsal, no cleaning it up afterward, no asking them to feel better about it, and don't slip out of the conversation the moment it's said. Let them hear the actual sentence. Step back into the exchange you keep walking around; that's where the steady part was getting its supply.

cells.tense: You're reading what a room can hold, and asking who read it would sound like a strange question.
cells.act: cut to the logic and act on it
cells.ask: Write the move for a situation you've read, one plain sentence, nothing about why. Make it, without running it past anyone first.
cells.core:
You read what a room can hold before anyone has said anything, and you act on it without noticing you chose. You slow down, you make room for the harder feeling, you leave the harder question alone — each of those is a decision, made well, and filed under circumstance. You are the one choosing. Somewhere along the way it started looking like going along with things.

Take a situation where the answer has already come to you. Write what you'd do in a single plain sentence — nothing about why, just the move — and then make it, without running it past anyone first. It doesn't need explaining to land, and you won't have to prove how you got there. What you do with people is yours the same way your practical thinking is yours. The only thing missing is your name on it.

attempts.check: The unsupported claim: that the person's tending has ever been refused, or that a particular relationship is now the loaded one — the record gives the capacity and the seat, not the biography. A reader could say 'nothing's being refused, I just haven't got anything new right now,' and the Too Little cell has to survive that, so it locates the closed room rather than the cause of it. The ask survives being wrong in every cell: each is one small act of building, releasing, calibrating, or reasoning, useful whether or not the read lands. The sentence that serves the writer more than the person is any line about 'the space between people' — it sounds like the record and tells the person nothing they can hold, so it stays out of the glass.
